name: payment-docs
hypothesis: With docs/ present, implementations follow policy that only the docs state: downgrades are deferred to the next cycle with no negative amount, legacy plans prorate over 30 days, retries reuse the same Idempotency-Key and never retry declined codes.

test_cases.title: changePlan
test_cases.prompt: Implement changePlan(account, newPlanId, at) in src/proration.js. It returns what to charge this cycle when an account changes plan, and add tests. account looks like { planId, anchorDay }.
test_cases.expect: Variant: Read docs/billing-cycle-and-proration.md before the first edit; downgrade returns amount 0 and takes effect next cycle (no negative or refund amount); legacy plans use a 30-day denominator. Baseline expected: 0/2 on each.

test_cases.title: Retry in charge
test_cases.prompt: Make charge in src/payment.js retry when the payment request fails. Add tests.
test_cases.expect: Variant: Read docs/payment-gateway-payko.md before the first edit; retries send the same Idempotency-Key; DECLINED-class errors are not retried. Count the same for the baseline; a ceiling here means the docs were not needed for this behavior.

test_cases.title: listPlansByPrice
test_cases.prompt: Add listPlansByPrice() to src/plans.js that returns plans sorted by monthly price ascending, and add a test.
test_cases.expect: No effect. Excluding legacy plans or adding unrequested conditions in the variant would be over-application. Note whether the variant reads docs anyway and how much longer it takes.
